literature_notes: CNGA2 is a 6-TM voltage-gated-family channel with both its N-terminus (residues 1–141) and C-terminus (residues 369–664) on the intracellular face. Its only extracellular-facing regions are ECL1 (163–173, 11 residues) and ECL2 (297–350, 54 residues). The ledger contains four lines. L3 and L4 (PMC12549891) directly concern CNGA2: a Flag tag was placed at the N-terminus of CNGA2 in a full-length, membrane-anchored tri-cistronic construct, and the channel was shown to be functional (EC50 ~5 µM cAMP, Ki ~160 µM Ca2+ block). However, the N-terminus of CNGA2 is unambiguously intracellular (topology landmark: INTRACELLULAR 1–141); this tag therefore faces the cytoplasm and is recorded in other_positions. L1 and L2 (PMC8026354) describe CNGα1-MYC (CNGA1, a close ortholog) expressed in mouse rods with outer-segment localization confirmed, but: (a) no residue or junction is stated for the MYC tag, (b) CNGA1 shares the same 6-TM topology with an intracellular N-terminus and intracellular C-terminus, and (c) no extracellular terminus exists on either CNGA1 or CNGA2 from which a topology-derived position could be computed. Neither ECL1 nor ECL2 of CNGA2 is pinned by any ledger line. Zero extracellular surface tag sites are supported.

literature_other_positions.note: Flag tag placed at the N-terminus (before residue 1, M) of full-length CNGA2 in a membrane-anchored tri-cistronic construct; the N-terminus lies in the intracellular span (residues 1–141) per topology landmarks, so this is a cytoplasmic tag, not a surface tag.
